# package secauth

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/secauth"
```

Package secauth implements the cryptographic core of DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5 (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7): the message authentication codes and the construction of the data they protect.

The procedures that use it are wired into the client and the server through their WithSecureAuthentication option: the challenge of critical requests (DefaultCritical by default), aggressive mode (AggressiveOverhead is what it adds to a request), the session key change and the security statistics ([Statistic](#type-statistic)), with HMAC-SHA-256 (which every SAv5 device must implement) or HMAC-SHA-1, and AES-128 or AES-256 key wrap (RFC 3394). Update keys are configured on both ends out of band: the update key change and user management procedures, and AES-GMAC, are not implemented.

## Constants

```go
const AggressiveOverhead = 32
```

AggressiveOverhead is the most an aggressive mode request adds to a request: the g120v3 object with its header (10 octets) and the g120v9 MAC with its header (6 octets and a MAC of up to 16).

```go
var DefaultCritical = []app.FunctionCode{

	app.FuncSaveConfiguration, app.FuncAssignClass, app.FuncOpenFile, app.FuncDeleteFile,
	app.FuncActivateConfig, app.FuncAuthenticateFile,

```

DefaultCritical are the function codes an outstation challenges by default, and a master sends in aggressive mode: the ones that change the outstation's state.

```go
var ErrKeyWrap = errors.New("secauth: key unwrap failed")
```

ErrKeyWrap reports wrapped key data that does not unwrap: a wrong key, damaged data, or data whose integrity check fails.

## Functions

### func AuthData

```go
func AuthData(challenge, criticalFragment []byte) []byte
```

AuthData is the data a challenge reply authenticates (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.5.2.1): the full challenge object as it was sent, followed by the critical application fragment that was challenged.

Both stations build it the same way, so the master's reply MAC and the outstation's verification MAC match when the key matches.

### func Equal

```go
func Equal(a, b []byte) bool
```

Equal reports whether the two MACs are equal, in constant time.

### func KeyChangeData

```go
func KeyChangeData(control, monitoring, keyStatus []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

KeyChangeData is the plaintext of a session key change (g120v6, IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.5.2.3): the length of a session key, the control direction and the monitoring direction session keys, and the key status message the outstation sent last, padded with zeros to a multiple of 8 octets for the key wrap.

### func KeyUnwrap

```go
func KeyUnwrap(kek, wrapped []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

KeyUnwrap reverses KeyWrap and checks the integrity value. A wrong key or damaged data fails with ErrKeyWrap.

### func KeyWrap

```go
func KeyWrap(kek, plaintext []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

KeyWrap wraps plaintext with the AES key wrap algorithm of RFC 3394 under kek (16 or 32 octets). plaintext must be a multiple of 8 octets and at least 16.

### func MAC

```go
func MAC(alg app.MACAlgorithm, key, data []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

MAC computes the message authentication code of data under key for the algorithm alg, truncated to the algorithm's length. It returns an error for an algorithm this package does not implement.

### func ParseKeyChangeData

```go
func ParseKeyChangeData(plain []byte, keyStatus ...[]byte) (control, monitoring []byte, err error)
```

ParseKeyChangeData returns the session keys of unwrapped key change data, after checking that it carries one of the given key status messages followed only by padding. Several forms are accepted because implementations differ in whether the key status message includes its MAC value.

## Types

### type Statistic

```go
type Statistic uint16
```

Statistic is the index of a security statistic (group 121, events in group 122), as IEEE 1815-2012 clause 7.6 numbers them.

```go
const (
	StatUnexpectedMessages Statistic = iota
	StatAuthorizationFailures
	StatAuthenticationFailures
	StatReplyTimeouts
	StatRekeysDueToAuthFailure
	StatTotalMessagesSent
	StatTotalMessagesReceived
	StatCriticalMessagesSent
	StatCriticalMessagesReceived
	StatDiscardedMessages
	StatErrorMessagesSent
	StatErrorMessagesReceived
	StatSuccessfulAuthentications
	StatSessionKeyChanges
	StatFailedSessionKeyChanges
	StatUpdateKeyChanges
	StatFailedUpdateKeyChanges
	StatRekeysDueToRestarts
	// NumStatistics is the number of statistics: indexes 0..NumStatistics-1.
	NumStatistics
)
```

The security statistics.

### type User

```go
type User struct {
	// Number is the user number; 1 is the default user. IEEE 1815-2012
	// reserves 0 for an unknown user: client.WithSecureAuthentication and
	// server.WithSecureAuthentication take 0 as 1.
	Number uint16
	// UpdateKey is the update key: 16 octets (AES-128 key wrap) or 32
	// octets (AES-256).
	UpdateKey []byte
	// Key is a pre-shared control direction session key, used when there
	// is no UpdateKey.
	Key []byte
	// MAC is the algorithm; zero selects HMAC-SHA-256 truncated to 16.
	MAC app.MACAlgorithm
}
```

User holds the keys and identity of one SAv5 user.

With an UpdateKey the session keys are negotiated by the session key change procedure: the master wraps fresh keys with the update key on every connection and at the key change interval. Without one, Key is a pre-shared control direction session key used directly.

#### func (User) Algorithm

```go

```

Algorithm returns the user's MAC algorithm, defaulting to HMAC-SHA-256-16.
